info.title: Fractal Flame API
info.description: Backend API for storing, searching, and serving fractal flame configurations

get.summary:
The audit log. Readable by **any** admin, not just the one who acted —
moderation that only its author can review isn't accountable to anyone.

post.summary: Block an email domain from registering.
post.description:
Operator-managed rather than a compiled-in list: a static blocklist goes
stale, and this gets used reactively — you add a domain when you see it.

Worth weighing before adding one: there is no appeal path, so a false
positive silently locks out every legitimate user of a small mail host with
no way for them to tell you.

get.description:
Reports from non-active accounts never appear here — they are stored as
evidence, not surfaced as work. The `entity_report_count` on each row
applies the same filter, so a brigade of shadowbanned accounts cannot make
something look more reported than it is.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Omit for every queued report regardless of state.

post.summary: Mark a report actioned or dismissed — or reopen it.
post.description:
Dismissing is a decision worth recording: a dismissed report and a
never-seen report are different facts, and only one of them means somebody
looked.

put.summary:
Feature/unfeature a room on the museum hub. Featuring requires a public,
visible room — the explore filter would hide a featured private room, and
a curation flag that silently does nothing is worse than a 400.
Map an entity type to its table.
put.description:
A closed match rather than interpolating the caller's string: this value
reaches a `format!`ed table name, and the only safe way to do that is for
every reachable value to be one we wrote.
Feature/unfeature a hall or branch and manage its museum slug — the UI
face of what used to be manual SQL. Featuring requires the script to be
published (an unfeatured-unpublished script fronts nothing anyway; a
featured one would promise a walk that 404s).

post.description:
Removes it from `/api/tags` and `/api/tags/popular` and refuses it on new
tagging. Existing `flame_tags` rows are untouched: the flames keep the
association and their authors see nothing change. Deleting associations
would fight the `usage_count` trigger and silently edit content that was
never itself the problem.

**This is the only way a display name can ever change.** It is set at
registration and `PUT /api/users/me/profile` deliberately does not touch it,
so a user cannot fix an offensive one even if they want to.

It also cannot be hidden, because it rides on every public thing the account
owns. Replacing it is the only available action, which is why this is a
rename rather than another moderation state.

The generated name derives from the account id, so renaming the same account
twice is idempotent rather than producing a trail of neutral names.

post.summary: Shadowban, hard-disable, or restore an account.
post.description:
Restoring is deliberately unremarkable: because content is hidden by a
filter on read rather than by rewriting rows, setting the state back to
`active` restores exactly what was there. Nothing has to remember what was
hidden.

post.summary: Hide, unhide or remove one piece of content.
post.description:
`entity_type` is validated against the same closed set the audit table's
CHECK enforces — an unknown type must not reach a `format!`ed table name.

Always `204`, whatever happens — unknown address, no mail provider
configured, send failure. This endpoint is unauthenticated, so any response
that varied with the outcome would be a free account-enumeration oracle:
post an address, learn whether it has an account here. That matters more
than the lost feedback, and honest UI copy ("if that address has an account,
a link is on its way") costs the user nothing.

The send is spawned rather than awaited for the same reason. Waiting on an
outbound HTTPS request only when the account exists would leak through
response time exactly what the status code refuses to say.

204.description: Accepted — reveals nothing about whether the account exists

post.summary: Send a fresh verification link, superseding any earlier one.
post.description:
Returns `204` whether or not anything was sent — including when the account
is already verified. A response that distinguished them would let a logged-in
account probe its own state in a way that is pointless to allow and awkward
once shadowbans exist.

post.summary: Consume a reset link and set a new password.
post.description:
No JWT is returned: the reset revokes every session for the account,
including any this request could have been handed, so the caller signs in
again with the new password. Returning a token here would mean minting one
in the same breath as invalidating them all — easy to get subtly wrong, and
it buys a single skipped login.

204.description: Password changed; all existing sessions revoked

post.description:
Unknown, expired and already-used tokens are all `404`. Distinguishing them
would confirm that a guessed token had once been real, which tells an
attacker they hit a live account.

200.description: Browse catalog — no shader or parameters
Flame with v2 config blob + root transforms

404.description: Flame not found or not forkable

200.description: Spot already existed; bookmarked for the caller

201.description: New spot — this save created it

204.description: Stored, or already present (first write wins)

403.description: Caller has not saved this item

post.description:
Returns `204` whether or not the report was new — see
`repositories::reports::create` for why the caller must not be able to tell.

get.summary:
Resolve a walk ref — an admin-assigned slug or a script UUID — to the
published pin. Slugs cap at 32 chars and UUIDs are 36, so the two forms
cannot collide; a ref is tried as UUID first only because the parse is
cheap and exact.

post.summary:
Publish (or re-publish) this script to the museum: a generator becomes a
Hall, a modifier becomes a Branch. Publishing PINS the current source —
the museum serves exactly that snapshot until the author presses publish
again, so halls and branches stay static under everyone's feet.
Copy a readable script into the caller's account.
post.description:
This is how a user starts from one of the built-in scripts: those are
imported as admin-owned rows so the site can browse them and the museum
can serve them, which leaves them read-only to everybody else.

The fork is **private** and unpublished regardless of the source's
visibility — a copy is not an endorsement to republish, and the owner can
flip it themselves once they have changed something.

Its name is chosen by the server (`<source>_fork`, then `_fork2`, ...) and
is guaranteed not to be a reserved stem, so a fork of a built-in is
something the client will actually load. The caller does not get to pick,
because the interesting failure — landing on a reserved name — is not one
they could be expected to anticipate.

201.description: Fork created, private to the caller

400.description: Script limit reached, or every candidate name is taken

404.description: No such script, or not readable

put.summary:
Replace the hall's presentation config and preview. Owner-only,
full-replace, no version gate — see `HallConfigRequest`.

400.description: Bad config shape or unknown preview item
Script not public, or email unverified

parameters.name: published
parameters.description:
`true` narrows to the museum: published scripts only, with `kind` and
`sort` applying. Halls are published generators, branches published
modifiers.

200.description: Current user's resource usage and limits

404.description: No library entry for this hash

200.description: List all available variations (lightweight; no shaders or parameter schema)

AddRoomItemRequest.description: Exactly one of the two — a wall position holds a gallery item or a flame.

AnimationRef.description: Lightweight reference to an animation — used in flame responses.

CreateFlamePalette.description:
Embedded palette in a flame request. `hash` is optional if `color_data`/
`stops` are present (server computes hash, upserts content); if no content
is provided, the server requires `hash` to already exist in `palette_data`.
`name` is the flame-specific display name, denormalized onto the flame row.

config.description:
Opaque to the server end-to-end. The Phase 2 dual-write path parses
this internally into `FlameConfigBlob` to populate the v1 typed
columns alongside the v2 JSONB column, but unknown fields the client
adds round-trip via the JSONB column untouched.

nickname.description: Nickname for the caller's bookmark of this item.

seed.description:
The DEFAULT seed (u64 decimal string) — every stage without a seed
of its own runs at this one. Seeds are positions on a ring of 2^64,
past what a JSON number can carry exactly. Identity is computed from
the RESOLVED per-stage seeds, so the same spot saved with a different
default converges on the same hash.

CreateGalleryItemResponse.description:
`created` distinguishes "you discovered this spot" from "someone was here
first" — the item exists identically either way, so re-POSTing is safe.

EffectDownload.description: Full detail for `GET /api/effects/{name}` — carries the WGSL.

parameters.description:
Served verbatim; see `EffectParameter`. Capped at 48 by
`effects_param_cap` — physical uniform capacity, not policy.

requires_blend_modes.description:
Whether the compiled shader needs the `// INCLUDE_BLEND_MODES` splice
of `shaders/effects/common/blend_modes.wgsl`.

shader.description:
NULL until the shader seed migration lands, which is exactly when
`downloadable` flips true.

EffectListItem.description:
Browse payload for `GET /api/effects`.

Same rule as `VariationListItem`: a field earns a place here if a
**browse-or-select decision** can be made from it. The shader is the whole
weight of the payload and is never needed to choose an effect, so it lives
on the detail endpoint only.

category.description:
The pipeline position — `density` runs before tonemap, `color` after.

Served as `category` to match the client's wire format and the
variation payload. It is the **same column** as `effect_stage`; there is
deliberately no second column, because an effect's category *is* its
stage (client §4.3: "exactly one category, `density` or `color`,
deciding pipeline position").

downloadable.description:
Whether a client may fetch and register this effect at runtime.

False for every row until the shaders are seeded — which is the honest
statement of the interim, rather than letting a client discover it by
fetching one and finding nothing to compile.

EffectParameter.description:
Documentation-only shape for one entry of `effects.parameters`.

As with `VariationParameter`, the server does **not** deserialize into
this — `EffectDownload.parameters` is served verbatim. The typed version of
the variation equivalent lost data twice (a dropped `description`, a 500 on
the externally-tagged enum form), and effects mirror that wire format
one-for-one, so they would inherit both.

Every value is an `f32` on the wire and in the uniform regardless of type;
`param_type` drives UI rendering only.

param_type.description: Either a bare string or externally tagged `{"enum": {"choices": [...]}}`.

FlamePalette.description:
Embedded palette in a flame response. Always carries the hash + the
flame's display name; content fields are populated from `palette_data`.

FlameResponse.description:
v2 wire response shape. Everything that's not identity / engagement /
palette lives inside `config` (the opaque JSON blob). Root-flame
transforms ride alongside `config` in their own array; subflames + their
transforms live INSIDE `config.subflames[]`.

render_mode.description:
Top-level mirror of `config.render_mode` so list + detail responses
have a consistent shape (FlameListItem already exposes it at the
top level). The same value also lives inside `config` for clients
that prefer to read it from the blob.

saved.description: Whether the CALLER has this item saved. Always false anonymous.

seed.description:
The HALL's seed, u64 as a decimal string (kept for list rows and
compatibility; each stage's own seed rides on its ref).

GalleryScriptInput.description:
One script the item depends on, as submitted: full source plus the
FULLY RESOLVED params (every declared param with the value actually passed
to the interpreter, defaults included — the hash must not depend on
whether a value was explicit or defaulted).

builtin_id.description:
Engine builtin id (`basic_random`, `mutate`, ...) when the source came
from the embedded engine scripts. Labeling only, not hashed.

script_id.description:
The script row the source came from, when it is a user script. Must be
readable by the caller — otherwise saving would attribute snapshots to
scripts the caller cannot see.

seed.description:
This stage's OWN seed (u64 decimal string), when it differs from the
request's default - a pinned stage of the walk. Absent = the default.

GalleryScriptRef.description:
A script reference in an item response: the snapshot inline (source and
all), plus the params this item runs it with.

script_id.description:
The script this snapshot came from, when known — what lets a client
rebuild a walkable ref for "Walk here" on published-script items.

seed.description:
This stage's resolved seed (u64 decimal string). Every stage of a
stored item is fully explicit — museum doc §15.

source.description:
The exact source that reproduces this item, verbatim from the
snapshot. Inline because re-running it is the entire point of the
fetch; by-ref would cost one round trip per script before the first
pixel.

HallConfigRequest.description:
Full-replace hall presentation update. Separate from the optimistic
script PUT on purpose: the editor app sends whole-script updates without
knowing this field exists, and riding along there would silently wipe it.
No version check — presentation metadata, single owner, last write wins.

hall_config.description:
Null clears. Shape: `{branches?: [ref], params?: [name], defaults?:
{tile?: {width?, height?, iterations?}, preview?: {...}}}`.

preview_item_hash.description: Null clears. Must be a visible gallery item.

reason.description:
Operator-facing note. Recorded in the audit log, never served to the
affected user — there is no appeal path.

ModerationState.description:
Operator's axis, orthogonal to `Visibility` (the owner's).

Both non-visible states keep the row and are reversible; the difference is
intent, recorded for triage. Neither is served to anyone but the owner and
admins.

PaletteContent.description:
Public palette content, returned by `GET /api/palettes/{hash}` and
embedded in flame responses.

display_name.description:
Omit to generate a neutral `user_<8 hex>` name derived from the account
id. Supply one to restore a previous name: the audit log records what it
was, and without a way to set it back a mistaken rename is permanent.

ReportResponse.description:
Triage payload.

Deliberately does not embed the reported entity. An admin's ordinary `GET`
already bypasses visibility and moderation state (`authorize_read`
returns early for admins), so the browser app fetches the target through the
same endpoint anyone else would — one code path, and no second projection of
four different resource types to keep in step.

entity_report_count.description:
How many reports this entity has, across all reporters.

The number that actually drives triage — one report is a signal, six is
a queue-jumper — and cheap to compute here rather than making the UI
issue a second pass.

state.description:
`actioned` or `dismissed`. Setting it back to `open` is allowed —
reopening a report someone closed too quickly is a real workflow.

ResolvedScriptResponse.description:
What the walk runs: a published script resolved by slug or UUID. `source`
is the PIN — the snapshot taken at publish time — not the script's current
source, so halls and branches stay static under everyone's feet.

hall_config.description:
The hall's presentation config — branches/params/defaults. The walk
needs it alongside the pin (mutable, unlike the pin).

RoomFlameRef.description: A flame hanging in a room.

RoomGalleryItemRef.description: A gallery item hanging in a room — enough to draw a tile from thumbnails.

RoomItemResponse.description:
One wall position. Exactly one of `gallery_item` / `flame` is set; a
position whose member the caller cannot see is omitted from the listing
entirely (re-filtered at read time, the collections convention).

preview_has_thumbnail.description: Whether that member actually has an uploaded thumbnail to show.

preview_item_hash.description:
The room's preview: its FIRST item (wall order), re-filtered like the
wall itself so a hidden member never fronts a public room. Exactly one
of the two refs is set when a preview exists.

SavedGalleryItem.description:
A row of the caller's saved list. Carries enough to render a thumbnail
grid without loading the WASM engine.

ScriptConflict.description:
Returned with `409 Conflict` when the submitted version is stale.

Carries enough for the client to decide between refetch-and-merge and
warn-the-user. Deliberately not the whole script — a client that wants the
current content can GET it, and a script's source can be 256 KB.

current_version.description: The version currently stored. Yours was older.

ScriptListItem.description:
Browse payload. Omits `source` — the whole weight of the record, and never
needed to decide whether you want a script.

owner_display_name.description:
The owner's display name.

Carried because `users.display_name` is case-insensitively unique
(migration 37), which makes `display_name/name` a globally unique,
stable, human-readable key — what a client needs to namespace two
authors' `grand_julian` on import without inventing a disambiguator or
showing a UUID fragment.

preview_has_thumbnail.description: Whether `preview_item_hash` has an uploaded thumbnail — what an entrance card actually needs to know before rendering an .

ScriptMuseumRequest.description:
Museum curation for a published script, both knobs together (they are
assigned together): whether it fronts the EFG entrance / branch lists,
and its short walk handle. `slug: null` clears — deliberate, audited.

forked_from.description:
The script this was forked from, or `NULL` for an original.

Attribution, not a dependency — a fork carries a full copy of
`source`, so `ON DELETE SET NULL` costs the lineage and nothing else.

source.description:
Authoritative. The client re-derives `display_name` / `kind` / `flags` /
`description` from this on load; a mismatch means our stored metadata is
stale, not that the script is wrong.

version.description: Send this back on PUT. See `UpdateScriptRequest::version`.

SnapshotResponse.description: Raw snapshot fetch, for clients that cache script sources by hash.

SubmitPaletteRequest.description:
Submit palette content. Server computes the hash from `color_data`+`stops`,
upserts into `palette_data`, and (if `nickname` is set) adds the palette
to the caller's library with that nickname.

nickname.description: If set, also adds the palette to the caller's library with this name.

SubmitPaletteResponse.description:
Response from `POST /api/palettes`. `added_to_library` is true when the
caller asked for `nickname` AND a new library entry was created (existing
entries are not overwritten — use the library endpoints for that).

TransformV2Wire.description:
What a single transform looks like on the wire — both in
`CreateFlameRequest.transforms[]` and `FlameResponse.transforms[]`.

`data` is opaque to the server end-to-end: stored as JSONB in
`transforms.data`, served back verbatim. The client owns the shape.

version.description:
The version you last read. **Required** — updates are optimistic.

A desktop app and a browser tab don't share a store, so last-write-wins
would silently discard whichever edit lost the race, with nothing to
notice it by. A stale version gets `409 Conflict` carrying the current
`version` and `updated_at`, so the client can refetch and merge rather
than guess.

UpsertUserPaletteRequest.description: `PUT /api/users/me/palettes/{hash}` body — adds or updates a library entry.

email_verified_at.description:
When the address was confirmed; `null` if it never was.

Serialised, unlike every other operator-facing field below. Verification
status is something the account legitimately needs to know about itself:
it gates publishing, so without this the browser app can only discover
it by attempting to publish and reading the `email_not_verified` error.
That is the difference between prompting someone to check their inbox
and letting them find out when their upload fails.

Timestamp rather than a bare boolean because it is what the column
holds; `null` is falsy in the one client that consumes it.

UserProfileResponse.description: API response combining user_profiles fields with display_name from users table.

UserState.description:
Account state. `shadowbanned` accounts authenticate and behave normally
from the inside; only other people stop seeing their content.

aliases.description:
Foreign-app names that resolve to this variation on `.flame` import
(Apophysis/JWildfire `linear3D` → our `linear`).

authors.description:
Historical attribution — the designers, in order. **Not** a foreign key
to `users`; these are people, not accounts.

description_plain.description:
`description` with markdown syntax stripped, for clients without a
markdown renderer. Absent falls back to showing `description` raw,
which degrades readably.

features.description:
The §6.1 capability array — **the only encoding of the thirteen flags**.

`needs_rng` / `needs_transform` / `writes_color` were separate boolean
columns until migration 82; they are now strings in here like the other
ten. An unrecognised name is dropped with a warning client-side rather
than rejecting the variation, so adding a capability is never a breaking
change in the server→client direction.

parameters.description:
Served **verbatim**. Nothing in the server reads inside it — the only
consumer of its structure is `jsonb_array_length(parameters)` in
`variations_param_slot_cap`, which is SQL. Parsing it here would add a
way to lose data and no way to gain any; see `VariationParameter` for
the two ways an earlier typed version did exactly that.

plot_emits.description:
`Feature::PlotEmits(u8)` — the one engine feature carrying a payload,
so it cannot ride the `features` string array.

`None` is the *only* encoding of absence. **`0` means "does not emit"**,
not "emits zero", so a stored `0` would be a second spelling of `None`
— and `plot_emits.is_some()`, which reads as "has the feature", would
be wrong for exactly that input. Migration 75 rejects it.

state_count.description:
Per-(thread, xform, variation) f32 slots persisted across the inner
iteration loop, paired with the WGSL that seeds them beyond zero-fill.

Uncapped: state lives in a separate buffer sized dynamically from the
flame, so it neither joins the packed-parameter sum nor needs a ceiling.

VariationListItem.description:
Lightweight shape used by `GET /api/variations`. Omits `parameters` and
the shader sources so a full catalog list stays small; clients hit
`GET /api/variations/{name}` for full data.

The bar for a field here is that a **browse/select decision** can be made
from it. Engine wiring (`phase`, `features`, `init_param_count`,
`state_count`) does not qualify — registration always happens from the
detail payload, so wiring on the list is bytes with no consumer, fetched for
the whole corpus under the manifest-driven catalog.

Five such fields were trimmed on 2026-07-31 after the client confirmed
nothing declares them and nothing uses `deny_unknown_fields`; three of those
no longer exist at all (migration 82). This shape is the client's documented
§2 plus `has_shader_3d` and `downloadable`.
See docs/api-shared-resources-server.md §1.2.

downloadable.description:
Whether a client may fetch and register this variation at runtime.

Not "has a shader". `subflame_wf` has a real 2D shader on the client —
it calls `subflame_iterate` and reads the subflame storage buffers —
it is simply **built-in-only by nature**, so there is nothing servable
to store. Saying `downloadable: false` states that truthfully while
keeping the row in the catalog for the browsing app and the panel.

Earns its place by the same rule as `has_shader_3d`: "don't try to
fetch this" is exactly a browse-or-select decision. It also underwrites
the download contract — **if it's downloadable, it has a shader the
client can use for its category**:

* any category → `shader_2d` required. A NULL there would reach the
  emit loop's `else { continue }` and silently contribute nothing.
* `only_3d` → `shader_3d` suffices. The engine removes these from the
  active set in 2D builds *before any source lookup*, so a 2D body is
  never read and requiring one would mean dead data that looks
  meaningful (migration 74).

One-directional: see `variations_downloadable_has_shader` for why a
shader won't stay *sufficient* either (name-gated helper libraries).

has_shader_3d.description:
Whether a dedicated 3D shader exists. Derived (`shader_3d IS NOT
NULL`), not stored.

Earns its place on the list because it drives a decision made *before*
download: the client's shader builder **skips a variation with no
`shader_3d` entirely** in 3D flames, so it contributes nothing and the
user meets it as a variation that renders blank. (The skip is
deliberate — an earlier 2D-pass-through fallback masked vec2/vec3
shader-validation crashes.) On the manifest the panel can mark it
"2D only" up front instead.

Contrast `shader_init`, which is deliberately *not* here: a missing
init shader has no valid form (the slots are allocated either way and
read as zeros), so it's a publish-time invariant — already enforced by
`variations_init_pair_check` — rather than something to advertise.

VariationParameter.description:
Documentation-only shape for one entry of `variations.parameters`.

**The server does not deserialize into this.** `Variation.parameters` is a
`serde_json::Value` served verbatim; this struct exists so the OpenAPI spec
still describes the shape. Round-tripping through a typed struct could only
lose data, and did: an earlier version omitted `description`, so all 3,231
per-parameter descriptions were silently dropped on read, and typed
`param_type` as `String`, which 500s on the 129 parameters whose type is
the enum object below.

description.description:
Per-parameter help text. Names like `hypergon`, `super_n3` and
`popcorn2_3D_c` are opaque without it.

param_type.description:
Either a bare string — `float`, `unlimited_float`, `integer`,
`unlimited_integer`, `boolean`, `angle` — or externally tagged
`{"enum": {"choices": [...]}}`. The authoritative list is
`param_types` in `docs/generated/engine-contract.json`.

Drives UI rendering and validation only, never storage: every value is
an `f32` on the wire and in the GPU buffer regardless of type.
